author: Aurochs1752
title: Fun puzzle game until it destroys your trust in the puzzles
content:
I really enjoyed Magic Sort for the first 100+ levels. It was interesting, relaxing, and just challenging enough to make you think. When I got stuck, I could assume I had made a mistake somewhere, try a different strategy, and eventually figure it out. That is exactly what I want from a logic puzzle game.

Then I reached Level 119.

After spending a significant amount of time carefully working through it, I eventually reached a complete dead end. I went back through the earlier decisions, considered alternative paths, and kept arriving at essentially the same problem: there simply wasn’t enough working space. The moment I finally used the “extra bottle” booster, the entire puzzle opened up and became a straightforward series of normal sorting moves.

That completely changed how I feel about the game.

The problem isn’t simply that a level is hard. I want hard levels. The problem is that now, whenever I get stuck, I can no longer know whether I made a mistake or the game intentionally gave me an unsolvable board unless I use a consumable booster.

That destroys one of the most important things a puzzle game needs: trust.

If I lose a chess game, fail a Sudoku, or get stuck on a good logic puzzle, I should be able to assume there is a solution within the rules. That is what makes it satisfying to keep thinking. If the answer might instead be “you were supposed to spend an extra-bottle item,” then there is little reason to spend 20 minutes analyzing where I went wrong. Maybe I didn’t go wrong at all.

Every normal level in this game should be solvable without a booster. If the designers want to create levels where an extra bottle is part of the intended mechanics, that’s fine but say so upfront. Label it something like “Extra Bottle Challenge” and provide the bottle as part of the level. Don’t present it as a normal “Super Hard” puzzle and allow the player to waste a huge amount of time searching for a clever solution that may not exist.

What makes this especially frustrating is that the booster didn’t just make Level 119 slightly easier. One additional bottle turned a deadlocked position into an almost obvious chain of clears. That makes it feel less like a difficult puzzle and more like a normal puzzle where one necessary piece of workspace was deliberately removed.

And now I have to assume there may be more levels like this ahead.

That’s why this bothers me much more than ads, difficulty spikes, or normal mobile-game monetization. Magic Sort was a genuinely enjoyable puzzle game. But once a puzzle game teaches the player that being stuck may be a monetization mechanic rather than a reasoning problem, it becomes hard to enjoy solving the puzzles at all.

I was having a great time with this game. Level 119 may be the level that makes me stop playing.

I’m not spending money just to get past a level, so I’m moving on to other puzzle games.

author: Marigold222
title: Difficult
content:
The game quickly becomes too difficult to be enjoyable. There are constant events running, most of which require win streaks to make any meaningful progress, but the difficulty level is too high to maintain a streak for more than a few levels. It constantly throws “super hard” levels at you, when the supposed normal difficulty ones can often be hard enough. It takes at least a few tries to beat a lot of levels. And then you only get 5 lives at a time that refill at a glacial place. 

Also many of the puzzles are purely luck based due to hidden colors. I’ve lost so many puzzles because there was no possible way for me to know I was about to enter a dead end. 

The difficulty level would be less frustrating if continues weren’t so expensive, if there wasn’t a lives system, and if events didn’t require crazy long win streaks. They’ve taken a cozy puzzle game and turned it into competition and stress.

The enginerd in me started screen recording the games to determine how many of the games failed because they weren't plausible and how many of them were because I made a wrong move. At least 30-40% aren't plausible to solve and that's giving the benefit of the doubt that the games that went 10+ moves before they failed were my fault. I get they programmed this into the algorithm because they want people to purchase features but who wants to spend time on a puzzle that's not even plausible to solve?
